item: Protected mode names the app to Wikimedia only: every other host gets the generic User-Agent (R657)
summary: R657, ruled on item 68's read. BEFORE: the Settings note, the user manual, docs/SECURITY.md and the settings endpoint's note said protected mode sends a generic User-Agent. The collector did (make_fetcher); a guarded session did not: _session_for set the caller's own agent before it read the mode, so every API client built on guarded_session (the statistics fetchers, OSM downloads and replication, self-update, the model installer, topic discovery, IPCC, the Wikidata and Wikipedia clients) named the app through the proxy. NOW: in protected mode a guarded session sends GENERIC_USER_AGENT to every host except Wikimedia's, whose User-Agent policy asks API clients to name themselves; those keep the caller's descriptive agent and still go through the proxy. The list is one constant, DESCRIPTIVE_AGENT_DOMAINS = wikipedia.org, wikidata.org, wikimedia.org (a host matches when it is one of them or ends with a dot and one of them; the dumps are dumps.wikimedia.org). keeps_descriptive_agent reads the host both ways requests and urllib3 read it, and both readings must be on the list, else the generic agent. The choice is made in GuardedSession.send, which requests calls for the first request and for every redirect hop, so a hop from Wikimedia to another host gets the generic agent and a User-Agent a request carried itself is replaced. Transparent mode is unchanged. TEXTS: the Settings note now says protected mode sends a generic User-Agent except to Wikimedia's sites (Wikipedia, Wikidata, the dumps), whose API policy asks each tool to name itself; the warning beside it no longer sends SOCKS users to an optional [safety] extra that does not exist (PySocks is core since R656) and says SOCKS proxies such as Tor need nothing extra installed; both keyed in all 12 locales. The option label (Protected, generic UA + proxy) is unchanged: the note directly above it states the exception. docs/USER_MANUAL.md, docs/SECURITY.md (with the constant and the redirect rule), the endpoint's note, the settings module docstring and docs/GOVERNANCE.md say the same. TESTS: tests/test_protected_user_agent_r657.py, 34: the list is exactly the three domains; eight Wikimedia URLs keep the agent; non-Wikimedia hosts and lookalikes (evilwikipedia.org, wikipedia.org.evil.example, wikidata.org.example, a sister project off the list, loopback) get the generic one, as do unreadable and ambiguous URLs; a real protected-mode session through a recording adapter sends the generic agent except to Wikimedia, replaces an agent the request carried, gives each redirect hop the agent its own host is owed, and a following session does the same; transparent mode names the app everywhere as before; the note and the warning are in index.html and in all 12 locales, and the old two keys are gone; each of the four texts states the exception. Against the base, 31 of 34 fail. NOT CHANGED, stated: the collector already sent the generic agent; a host that refuses a browser-like agent now refuses protected-mode requests (none of the hosts the app calls is known to); separate circuits still do not make Wikidata lookups unlinkable (68(b)). Release-notes line: «In protected mode the app no longer names itself to the sites it downloads data from: every site except Wikimedia's (Wikipedia, Wikidata, the dumps), which ask each tool to name itself, now gets a generic User-Agent.»
